analysis: Examined the PR: .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml (patch hunks at ~129-142 and ~166-176), changelog.d/desktop-release-sign-dmg.md, and docs/operations/desktop-release.md. The workflow now codesigns the DMG with the existing Developer ID (CSC_NAME, KEYCHAIN_PATH from the earlier import step) with a timestamp before notarytool submit and stapling. The verify step adds codesign --verify, a TeamIdentifier equality check against APPLE_TEAM_ID, and a spctl check requiring 'source=Notarized Developer ID' for the DMG. This tightens release integrity: the DMG's signing team is now checked and Gatekeeper acceptance is enforced. No new secrets, permissions, inputs or network surface. Fail-closed behavior holds under set -euo pipefail: a codesign failure aborts, and a grep mismatch on the tee'd spctl output aborts. The signing step runs before the always() keychain deletion, so key availability is unchanged. The doc and changelog edits are descriptive and match the code. The change is outside the provider runtime threat model (TB-002 WebSocket, TB-009 attestation, TB-011 App Attest, key custody A-002/A-003, cache T-041); it touches only desktop app distribution. It is adjacent to binary integrity (T-013, A-011), but the provider CLI binary, the hash registry and the qualification records (A-017) are unchanged. Unverified items: that CSC_NAME and KEYCHAIN_PATH are exported in that step's environment (outside the visible excerpt), and the actual runtime behavior of electron-builder DMG output and stapling, which only a workflow run can confirm. Neither is a security regression, since failure would break the release rather than weaken a check. The integration source omitted 2 units. The workflow file's full head text was not supplied, so only the patch hunks were reviewed. No findings.
